name: [R30] Single account/session seen from many distinct source IPs in a short window (proxy rotation)
message:
Exploratory heuristic for the "rotating egress IP" pattern described on attacker infrastructure Hunt.io tied to a campaign against seven South Korean banks (2026-11-04): alongside the R29 JNDI/LDAP toolset, the exposed relay hosted a proxy pool of ~79 distinct egress IPs. Hunt.io did not confirm this pool's direct role in the bank breaches -- this rule targets the general technique (spreading one account/session's traffic across many source IPs to evade per-IP rate limits and blocklists), not this one campaign.

Needs SIEM-side aggregation: group by account/session, short window, alert on distinct source-IP count exceeding your baseline. Large NAT pools, mobile roaming, and known VPN/monitoring services can look similar -- tune before trusting this alone.

cases.name: Single account authenticated from an unusually high number of distinct source IPs in a short window (needs SIEM-side baseline tuning -- see rule message)
